label: fiction
title: Eighteen Minutes Fast
setting: The present-day city of Aster Reach, where an overnight evidence-store alarm has ended with an officer dead and a municipal technician accused.
charge: murder of an on-duty police officer
elements: The accused caused the on-duty officer’s death.
The accused intended to kill or cause really serious injury.
The killing was not legally justified or excused.
hook: A camera appears to show Lena Voss leaving the evidence store after Officer Dax Mere was killed. The image is genuine, the face is hers, and its time seems decisive.

accused.human: Lena Voss repairs municipal alarm systems and cares for her father between overnight callouts.
accused.if_guilty: A conviction would imprison her for life and formally name her as the person who murdered an officer responding to duty.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: The accused entered the evidence store after midnight following an angry dispute with Officer Mere. A secure camera then placed her at the scene after his death, and she concealed that visit. The prosecution says the genuine image, her access record, and her own lie identify the person who deliberately killed him.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The camera does show Lena Voss, but it does not show her after the killing. An isolated recorder displayed a clock eighteen minutes fast. Independent transit records place Lena across the city when Officer Mere died. The prosecution has mistaken an authentic face beneath a false time for proof of murder.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Lena entered secretly, argued with Officer Mere, and initially denied being there. The archive camera captured her face and uniform. The defence asks you to treat every awkward fact as coincidence. Taken together, the access, dispute, concealment, and image establish identity, intention, and an unlawful killing beyond reasonable doubt.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Suspicion cannot repair a broken timeline. The recorder’s own restart log proves its display was eighteen minutes fast, while two independent transit systems place Lena away before the verified time of death. Her lie concealed an unauthorized repair, not murder. The prosecution cannot identify the killer beyond reasonable doubt.

epilogue: Lena Voss was acquitted. An independent inquiry separated the archive recorder from the city time network and reopened the unidentified-offender investigation. Officer Dax Mere’s family received a corrected public account stating that the last clear image of Lena preceded his arrival. Lena returned to alarm work months later, but she no longer accepts solitary night callouts.

cast.name: Lena Voss
cast.role_label: the accused and municipal alarm technician

cast.name: Eren Solt
cast.role_label: patrol officer and former partner of the deceased

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: The archive camera displays 1:31 a.m. as Lena Voss crosses the lobby in her orange work coat. The image is clear and unaltered. Prosecutors place Officer Mere’s death at 1:20 a.m., so the displayed time appears to show Lena leaving eleven minutes after the killing. Her face, service bag, and reflective coat stripe all appear plainly in the frame.
beats.reveal_note: The face was genuinely Lena’s, but the recorder clock was eighteen minutes fast. The image was captured at 1:13 a.m., before Officer Mere arrived.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: When did Officer Mere tell you he was going to the archive?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: At 1:16 a.m. Dispatch sent him to the silent alarm, and his body camera connected at 1:18 a.m.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Had he mentioned Lena Voss that evening?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: Yes. He said he intended to question her about an unauthorized repair entry and had sounded unusually concerned.

beats.text: When did Officer Mere tell you he was going to the archive? At 1:16 a.m. Dispatch sent him to the silent alarm, and his body camera connected at 1:18 a.m. Had he mentioned Lena Voss that evening? Yes. He said he intended to question her about an unauthorized repair entry and had sounded unusually concerned.
beats.reveal_note: The evidence establishes a reason for questioning Lena, but it does not place her with Officer Mere or identify his killer.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you hear Officer Mere speak to the person inside?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. The body-camera sound contains only the alarm and an indistinct voice.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Can you identify Lena from that voice or the dark figure?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. I cannot identify the figure or the voice. The figure’s face is never visible, and the voice contains no name.

beats.text: Did you hear Officer Mere speak to the person inside? No. The body-camera sound contains only the alarm and an indistinct voice. Can you identify Lena from that voice or the dark figure? No. I cannot identify the figure or the voice. The figure’s face is never visible, and the voice contains no name.
beats.reveal_note: The officer gave a careful and important limitation: the recording of the fatal encounter contains no usable identification.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: The city access register records Lena’s service card opening the archive at 12:47 a.m. She did not record the visit on her work sheet and first told investigators she had stayed home. The entry proves she visited the building and then concealed that visit. No later entry under Lena’s card appears, and the lobby exit required no card.
beats.reveal_note: Lena’s concealment damaged her credibility, but the accurate access time still placed her inside more than half an hour before the death.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What do the original transit records show?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Lena’s registered pass opened East Quay gate at 1:16 a.m., and the departing carriage camera shows her face at 1:19 a.m.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Are those systems linked to the archive recorder?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. Both use the central time service. We checked each against the same network record, and neither required a correction.

beats.text: What do the original transit records show? Lena’s registered pass opened East Quay gate at 1:16 a.m., and the departing carriage camera shows her face at 1:19 a.m. Are those systems linked to the archive recorder? No. Both use the central time service. We checked each against the same network record, and neither required a correction.
beats.reveal_note: Two independent records place Lena entering public transport away from the archive immediately before the verified fatal encounter.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: A pass can be carried by another person, correct?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Yes, but the carriage image shows Lena using it.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Could that image have been recorded earlier?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. The carriage location and central timestamp agree for that journey. The original file contains continuous footage before and after Lena boarded. No gaps, edits, or clock jumps are present.

beats.text: A pass can be carried by another person, correct? Yes, but the carriage image shows Lena using it. Could that image have been recorded earlier? No. The carriage location and central timestamp agree for that journey. The original file contains continuous footage before and after Lena boarded. No gaps, edits, or clock jumps are present.
beats.reveal_note: The cross-examination tested both substitution and timing. The witness gave direct, unqualified answers that preserved the alibi.

beats.speaker: dc
beats.text: The archive recorder restarted after a power interruption at 10:04 p.m. Its service log states that the local clock resumed eighteen minutes fast because time synchronization was disabled. Subtracting that offset changes the lobby image from 1:31 a.m. to 1:13 a.m. The machine wrote that entry automatically, several hours before the fatal alarm.
beats.reveal_note: This contemporaneous machine log resolves the apparent contradiction: Lena left before the officer arrived, and the displayed 1:31 time was false.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you enter the archive without recording the job?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I had caused the alarm fault during an earlier repair and returned to correct it before my supervisor learned.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: When did you leave?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: At about 1:13 a.m. I went directly to East Quay and boarded the next carriage. I was alone, and I kept my coat.

beats.text: Why did you enter the archive without recording the job? I had caused the alarm fault during an earlier repair and returned to correct it before my supervisor learned. When did you leave? At about 1:13 a.m. I went directly to East Quay and boarded the next carriage. I was alone, and I kept my coat.
beats.reveal_note: Her account is independently matched by the corrected archive time, the gate record, and the carriage image.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You lied when investigators first asked whether you had visited, did you not?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes. I feared losing my job for hiding the faulty repair.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Was Officer Mere investigating that misconduct?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes, but I had already left before he arrived. The transit records show exactly when and where I departed.

beats.text: You lied when investigators first asked whether you had visited, did you not? Yes. I feared losing my job for hiding the faulty repair. Was Officer Mere investigating that misconduct? Yes, but I had already left before he arrived. The transit records show exactly when and where I departed.
beats.reveal_note: The lie gave Lena a reason to avoid scrutiny, but it did not overcome the independent timeline or identify her as the killer.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: You must decide whether the prosecution has proved that Lena Voss was the person who killed Officer Mere and intended death or really serious injury. Lena does not have to prove where she was. If the corrected timeline leaves a reasonable possibility that she had departed, your verdict must be Not Guilty. That possibility is sufficient.
beats.reveal_note: The direction keeps the central question precise: an unexplained death and a suspicious lie do not prove the accused’s identity beyond reasonable doubt.

twist: The prosecution’s clearest image was authentic but mistimed. It captured Lena leaving before Officer Mere arrived; the recorder alone was eighteen minutes fast, while centrally timed transit records placed her elsewhere during the killing.

jurors.label: Night-shift baker
jurors.persona: Trusts a clear image first, then revises firmly when a clock error is proved.

agree: That clear lobby image looks like Lena leaving after the officer died.
pushback: A visible face is not enough if the time printed beneath it is wrong.
concede: The transit image changes my view because it shows Lena elsewhere at the verified time.
burden_drift: Lena should have to explain every minute because she lied about the visit.
burden_correct: Her lie raises suspicion, but the prosecution still has to identify the killer.
final: The corrected clock and the transit record leave me with reasonable doubt.

jurors.label: Records clerk
jurors.persona: Compares source clocks and gives independent records more weight than copied displays.

agree: The access register reliably proves Lena entered the building that night.
pushback: Entry at 12:47 does not establish presence at 1:20.
concede: The restart log provides a precise correction rather than a speculative one.
burden_drift: The missing work sheet makes me expect a complete account from Lena.
burden_correct: The official records must be tested by the prosecution’s burden, not by suspicion.
final: The centrally timed records place Lena away from the archive when the officer arrived.

jurors.label: Retired teacher
jurors.persona: Keeps the presumption of innocence visible when the room reacts emotionally.

agree: The defence account agrees with records created before anyone was accused.
pushback: No witness can identify Lena in the recording of the fatal encounter.
concede: I accept that her first lie was serious, although it does not prove murder.
burden_drift: Her concealment tempts the room to demand that she prove innocence.
burden_correct: The judge’s direction requires the prosecution to eliminate the reasonable timeline.
final: I remain Not Guilty because identity has not been proved.

jurors.label: Vehicle mechanic
jurors.persona: Accepts machine evidence when the fault and its measured effect are plainly demonstrated.

agree: A secure camera is useful evidence when its clock is working.
pushback: This recorder restarted badly, so its displayed time cannot be trusted.
concede: Eighteen minutes explains the whole apparent conflict without guesswork.
burden_drift: Lena created the alarm fault, so part of me expects her to solve the case.
burden_correct: Causing a fault is not the same as causing a death.
final: The proved clock error moves me to Not Guilty.

jurors.label: Shop manager and foreperson
jurors.persona: Organizes the discussion around what each record proves and does not prove.

agree: We agree that Lena entered and concealed the unauthorized visit.
pushback: We must separate that misconduct from the later killing.
concede: The sequence is clear once the archive time is corrected.
burden_drift: The room is starting to treat Lena’s lie as a duty to prove innocence.
burden_correct: The judge said the prosecution must prove identity beyond reasonable doubt.
final: Our decision turns on 1:20, and the reliable records place Lena elsewhere.

jurors.label: Apprentice electrician
jurors.persona: Moves quickly with vivid evidence but understands how power faults disrupt isolated equipment.

agree: At first, the face and the printed 1:31 time looked decisive to me.
pushback: A camera can record a true picture while displaying a false clock.
concede: The restart log makes the eighteen-minute error concrete.
burden_drift: Because Lena hid the repair, I keep wanting her to remove every doubt.
burden_correct: The prosecution must remove reasonable doubt; Lena does not carry that task.
final: I now read the image as proof that Lena left before the killing.

jurors.label: Network technician
jurors.persona: Changes position when independent systems expose a mistaken shared assumption.

agree: The lobby frame is authentic, and that initially supported guilt.
pushback: Authenticity of the image does not authenticate the recorder’s clock.
concede: The independent time sources prove that my first reading was wrong.
burden_drift: Lena’s dishonesty makes an unsupported inference feel safer than it is.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove the fatal encounter, not merely an earlier visit.
final: The verified systems put Lena on the carriage before Officer Mere entered.

jurors.label: Community nurse
jurors.persona: Listens closely to witness limits and refuses to turn suspicion into identification.

agree: Officer Solt was clear that the fatal recording identifies nobody.
pushback: The prosecution is joining an earlier clear face to a later unclear figure.
concede: I accept that Lena’s lie was damaging, but the reason she gave is independently supported.
burden_drift: A terrible death can make any unexplained conduct feel like guilt.
burden_correct: The seriousness of the charge makes accurate identification more important, not less.
final: I cannot identify Lena as the person who killed Officer Mere.

jurors.label: Warehouse supervisor
jurors.persona: Dislikes concealed workplace mistakes and is vulnerable to shifting the burden.

agree: Lena’s hidden repair gave Officer Mere a reason to question her.
pushback: A workplace cover-up still does not identify a murderer.
concede: The transit sequence is too specific for me to dismiss.
burden_drift: Lena lied first, so I want her to prove who else was inside.
burden_correct: That is the wrong burden; the prosecution must prove Lena was the killer.
final: I dislike her conduct, but I am not satisfied of murder.

jurors.label: Music student
jurors.persona: Notices rhythm and sequence, but initially follows whichever account sounds most immediate.

agree: I initially followed the simple story that the camera showed her leaving afterward.
pushback: The simple story uses the wrong time, so it cannot stay simple.
concede: The gate, carriage, and corrected recorder now form one clear sequence.
burden_drift: I keep thinking Lena should fill the gap because she was dishonest.
burden_correct: The gap belongs to the prosecution’s case, not Lena’s defence.
final: The reliable sequence leaves Lena away from the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Library assistant
jurors.persona: Separates what each source actually says and remains careful about missing proof.

agree: The service log and transit records support one another without sharing a clock.
pushback: The prosecution’s image proves Lena’s identity but not the alleged time.
concede: I concede that her initial denial was a proper reason for investigation.
burden_drift: It is easy to ask Lena for an answer because the real killer is unknown.
burden_correct: An unknown killer does not reduce the prosecution’s burden of proof.
final: The evidence proves an earlier visit, not the charged murder.
